context: a letter from George Bentham, which you are answering
exchanges:
Would you oblige me by telling me if you know of anything worth looking at for or against or upon your views of the Origin of species which may have appeared abroad—besides what Asa Gray or A. De Candolle have written— I do not mean mere reviews or analysis of your work such as those of the Revue des Deux Mondes etc—but any original observations or rational discussion— Have the Germans taken up the subject? I believe Decaisne’s memoir on the variation of species derived chiefly from the observation of cultivated fruits—and Naudin’s on hybrids which contains I believe a great deal of important matter are neither of them yet published

Yours very sincerely | George Bentham

I have run my eye over the Reviews & Notices on the Origin (amounting to about 90!) & very few are worth your notice.

Pictet’s is about the most valuable from the man’s knowledge.

Bronn wrote a final chapter, at my request, with excellent objections, in his German Edition, which I have tried partly to answer in the 3d. Edition of Origin p. 133–143

There is a favourable & long Review in Revue Germanique, which is important from coming from so good observer, as Claparede.

Much has been published in Germany but not worth your attention.

Of English I suppose you know Hopkins in Fraser, one of most important.

One of very best & partly Botanical is by Mr Maw in Zoologist.

There is one by Dr. Dawson in Canadian Naturalist, which, however, seems to me poor.—

There is good one in Calcutta Review.—

Of course these are not all worth your looking at, but as Book Post is so cheap, & as it may save you trouble, I send the lot.

Please be careful of them, & let me have them back, as soon as you have made any use of them

Believe me | Yours very sincerely | Ch. Darwin
